clue.text: Mediterranean island discovered by some with a camera

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tourist photographs an island that only a few visitors have found.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'discovered' in the definition, but an island is not 'discovered' as a name for it; 'discovered by' is the link, and 'some' signals that the island sits inside 'with a camera'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, home of Odysseus.

clue.text: Language student female's expecting at farm?

parts.note: Inca, the Quechua language of the Inca people
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A language student on a farm placement turns out to be pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of a cow carrying young, so pregnant in farmyard terms.

clue.text: Harry even catches broadcast somewhere in the Midlands

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Harry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: the poetic word for even takes the scattering verb inside it

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even
to sow seed is to broadcast it by scattering

explanation.surface: Harry even picks up a radio broadcast somewhere in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Halesowen is a town in the West Midlands, near Birmingham.

clue.text: Constant battle getting capital to save large plant

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant such as the speed of light
Ypres was the site of several First World War battles

indicators.note: a capital is the leading letter, here of save

explanation.surface: Constant warfare means the capital must be saved.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall evergreen conifer, so a large plant.

clue.text: Unknown pots, first seen at back, most attractive

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic unknown

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for pots is shifted to its end

parts.note: pots are pot bellies, so tummies

explanation.surface: Someone ranks a collection of unidentified pottery, judging the most appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first seen at back' moves the T of TUMMIES to the end, giving UMMIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, delicious or appealing things are described as yummy, so the superlative means most attractive.

clue.text: Bone fish, removing head, but keeping tail ultimately

indicators.note: the beheaded fish holds that letter inside it
remove the first letter of the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of tail

explanation.surface: Gutting a fish: cut off the head but leave the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: TUNA less its head is UNA, which keeps L, tail's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two forearm bones, on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Norma, in reality, hurt in outside lavatory shown as 'Vacant'

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt

indicators.note: the emptied lavatory sits outside the word in
vacant means emptied, so only the outer letters of lavatory remain

explanation.surface: Norma, in fact, was injured in an outdoor toilet marked 'Vacant'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacant' leaves L and Y from lavatory; they go round IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma Jeane Mortenson became the screen star Monroe; the clue reverses birth and stage name playfully.

clue.text: Horseplay?

parts.note: read not as rough fun but as a play about horses: Peter Shaffer's drama of a boy who blinds horses, with a Latin horse title

explanation.surface: Rowdy fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaffer's 1973 stage play is named with the Latin word for horse.

clue.text: Folk-rock band — they would include bass on certain tracks?

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits on top of the second
the pronoun takes the letter for bass inside it

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for bass in music
roads, abbreviated RDS, are one kind of track

explanation.surface: A band would use bass guitar on some of their recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracks' looks like songs on an album; here it means roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s American group, known for Mr Tambourine Man, pioneered folk-rock.

clue.text: Religious leader given a kiss in church

indicators.note: in places the letters for 'a kiss' inside those for church

parts.note: a kiss can be called a lip, as in a smacker on the lips

explanation.surface: A cleric receives a kiss during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the chief civil and religious ruler of the Muslim world, successor to Muhammad.

clue.text: Bernice regularly taking course in culinary style

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the name Bernice

parts.note: a course is a route or way taken

explanation.surface: A woman called Bernice attends a cookery class regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of Bernice, ENC.
explanation.definitionFit: French for wrapped in pastry and baked, a cooking style such as beef Wellington.

clue.text: Entertainment centre's star visiting young girl

indicators.note: the star is staying inside the girl's letters, as a visitor stays in a house

parts.note: a lass is a young girl
Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A celebrity performer drops in on a young fan at a showbusiness venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is famous for casinos and shows, a hub of gambling and entertainment.

clue.text: Religious community remains, some days, withdrawn

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the month's abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: MAR is short for March, a month and so some days

explanation.surface: A religious group's remnants, some days, keep to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu hermitage or retreat where a spiritual group lives together.

clue.text: County borders featured in Surrey magazine

parts.note: Glos is the abbreviation for Gloucestershire, an English county

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, here of Surrey

explanation.surface: A local magazine in Surrey runs a feature on the county's boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes S and Y, the first and last letters of Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is an expensive magazine printed on shiny paper.

clue.text: Scottish swimmer and runner acquiring instant energy

indicators.note: the runner gets the word for instant inside it

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow
a mo is a moment, an instant
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Scottish swimmer and a runner suddenly get a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: An Arbroath smokie is a Scottish smoked haddock; the surface swimmer is a fish, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoked haddock from the Angus coast, so a fish from Scotland.

clue.text: Club's rejected elements of One Direction in possession of joint

indicators.note: the two words hold the joint between them

parts.note: west is a compass direction
one as in at one, joined together: united; the band's words are rejected, taken in the opposite order, so this comes second
ham is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A football club turns down members of the boy band One Direction who were caught with a joint of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a British boy band; its two words are clued separately and 'rejected' swaps their order. The 's stands for 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the East London football club, an example of a club.

clue.text: Bug found in container with Eastern fruit

indicators.note: the word for bug is found inside the container

parts.note: a tin is a container
to bug is to annoy, to anger

explanation.surface: An insect turns up in a crate of imported oriental fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned citrus like a mandarin, so a fruit.

clue.text: Drill with lead put on skip

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: the lead in a film is its star
to skip is to jump

explanation.surface: A drill instruction: attach the lead and skip.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym exercise jumping with limbs spread, part of a fitness drill.

clue.text: Spinner, new resident in tiny mill town

indicators.note: the letter for new lives inside the word for tiny

parts.note: toy describes a very small breed of dog, so tiny
Blackburn is a Lancashire town built on cotton mills

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler newly moves into a small northern mill town.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinner is a disc jockey, who spins records, not a bowler. Tony Blackburn is a veteran British radio DJ; Blackburn is a former cotton town in Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blackburn was the first voice on BBC Radio 1, a record-playing disc jockey.

clue.text: Australian community involved in dance session

indicators.note: the two short pieces are put inside the dance

parts.note: bop is to dance
Oz is a nickname for Australia
EU, the European Union, was once the European Community

explanation.surface: An Australian group joins in a dance session.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy drinking session; the colloquial sense of session as a drinking bout.

clue.text: Idealistic Spaniard, dismissing judge, entertaining to detective

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means holding it inside, so the name surrounds the other pieces
the judge letter is sent away from the name

parts.note: Juan is a typical Spanish name
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A naive Spaniard, having fired the judge, hosts a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing judge' leaves UAN from JUAN, and TOPI goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: From More's imaginary perfect island, the word means idealistic or visionary.

clue.text: Main French coastal location, not one where spirits are raised?

parts.note: the main is the open sea

indicators.note: not says the numeral one is taken out of the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The sea at a French resort, missing just one thing for raising the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits are raised' suggests a holiday mood; here the spirits are ghosts called up.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a gathering where a medium tries to summon the dead.

clue.text: Animal's stink stifling another one

indicators.note: one smell smothers the other by surrounding it

parts.note: to reek is to stink, and a reek is a stench
BO, body odour, is another kind of stink

explanation.surface: An animal's stench overpowers a rival smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok is a small South African antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Residue seen on 5/11 and the majority of that month

indicators.note: the majority means most of the month's letters, its last five of eight

parts.note: the 11 in 5/11 is the eleventh month

explanation.surface: Leftovers from Bonfire Night, the fifth of November, and most of that month.
explanation.walkthrough: 5/11 is the British way of writing 5 November, Guy Fawkes or Bonfire Night, when bonfires and fireworks are lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing fragment left in a dying fire, typical after Bonfire Night.

clue.text: In understanding energy, advanced fuel can be created

indicators.note: In puts the word for advanced inside the letters for understanding plus energy

parts.note: ken is knowledge or understanding, as in beyond my ken
rose means went up or advanced
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics lesson: with grasp of energy, a better fuel could be made.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSE goes inside KENE, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin, a lamp and jet oil, is a fuel distilled from petroleum.

clue.text: Rock band given central stages in Dublin? Sure

indicators.note: the central letters of each of the two words are taken

explanation.walkthrough: 'central stages' takes BL from Dublin and UR from Sure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Britpop group fronted by Damon Albarn is a rock band.

clue.text: Top-class doctor in France to go back for protection against sun?

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: back reads the French verb from right to left

parts.note: aller is the French verb to go, flagged by 'in France'

explanation.surface: An eminent physician returns to France for help against sunburn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALLER into RELLA. The definition's question mark admits that this item is usually thought of as protection from rain, but a parasol works against the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol-type canopy held overhead shields from sun or rain.

clue.text: Intention is to switch over fourth episode of Planet of the Apes

indicators.note: switch over says the letters for intention and is are turned round

parts.note: an aim is an intention

indicators.note: the fourth episode, or part, of Planet is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A TV fan plans to change channels for the fourth episode of the Planet of the Apes series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to switch over' reverses AIMIS to SIMIA. 'fourth episode of' takes N, the fourth letter of Planet; the definition is the film title's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Simian is the adjective for monkeys and apes, so it means of the Apes.

clue.text: Saucy stuff from repellent one with cleavage repeatedly showing

indicators.note: repeatedly says the reversed piece appears twice
repellent things drive back, so the letters for one with cleavage are driven back into reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rip is a cleaving, a tear

explanation.surface: A racy display of cleavage from someone off-putting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repellent' reverses IRIP to PIRI, and 'repeatedly' doubles it. 'Saucy stuff' is literally a sauce, not something risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chilli sauce from Portuguese African cooking, so literally saucy stuff.

clue.text: News earlier disrupting part of hospital wing

indicators.note: the new letters break into the hospital department's pair

parts.note: A and E is the accident and emergency department
N is new, and NN serves as its plural, as PP does for pages
ex means former, earlier

explanation.surface: Earlier reports of upheaval in one hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E is the British name for a hospital's emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: A building added onto a main one, an extension or wing.
